This file implements the core logic for handling book steps in the XRPL payment and offer crossing engine. The main class, BookStep (templated on input/output types and a derived class), represents a step in a payment or offer path that traverses an order book, which can be either a central limit order book (CLOB) or an Automated Market Maker (AMM). BookStep manages offer consumption, quality calculation, transfer rates, and caching of results for both forward and reverse path calculations. It provides mechanisms to iterate over offers, apply transfer fees, handle self-crossing offers, and enforce path and issuer constraints. Two main derived classes, BookPaymentStep and BookOfferCrossingStep, specialize behavior for payment and offer crossing flows, respectively, including logic for quality thresholds and self-crossing prevention. The file also includes helper functions for constructing the appropriate BookStep variant based on the context and asset types, as well as test utilities for equality checks. The implementation is highly generic and modular, supporting both IOU and XRP asset types, and integrates with the ledger's view and sandboxing mechanisms to ensure correctness and consistency during transaction execution.

This header file defines the STTx class, which represents a signed transaction in the XRP Ledger protocol. The class inherits from STObject and CountedObject, and encapsulates transaction data, type, and ID. It provides constructors for various initialization methods, including from serialized data and custom assembly functions. The class supports single and multi-signature transactions, with methods for signing, signature verification, and extracting transaction details such as type, sequence, mentioned accounts, and transaction ID. It also includes methods for JSON serialization, SQL metadata generation, and batch transaction handling. The file defines transaction SQL status enums, and provides utility functions for local checks, transaction sterilization, and pseudo-transaction identification. The design enforces canonical signatures and supports protocol rule checks for expanded signer lists.

This file implements a set of invariant checks for the XRPL (XRP Ledger) transaction processing engine. Each class represents a specific invariant that must be maintained during ledger state transitions caused by transactions. The invariants ensure the integrity, consistency, and security of the ledger by validating that certain conditions hold before and after transactions are applied. Key invariants include: ensuring transaction fees are non-negative and within limits (TransactionFeeCheck), preventing the creation of XRP out of thin air (XRPNotCreated), checking for valid account balances (XRPBalanceChecks), disallowing invalid offers (NoBadOffers), ensuring escrow amounts are valid (NoZeroEscrow), preventing unauthorized account deletions (AccountRootsNotDeleted, AccountRootsDeletedClean), ensuring ledger entry types are consistent (LedgerEntryTypesMatch), disallowing XRP trust lines (NoXRPTrustLines), enforcing correct freeze semantics on trust lines (NoDeepFreezeTrustLinesWithoutFreeze, TransfersNotFrozen), validating new account creation (ValidNewAccountRoot), checking NFT page structure and NFT mint/burn counts (ValidNFTokenPage, NFTokenCountTracking), validating clawback operations (ValidClawback), ensuring correct issuance and management of multi-party tokens (ValidMPTIssuance), enforcing permissioned domain and DEX rules (ValidPermissionedDomain, ValidPermissionedDEX), and maintaining Automated Market Maker (AMM) pool invariants (ValidAMM). Each class provides visitEntry methods to observe ledger changes and finalize methods to enforce the invariant after transaction application, logging fatal errors and rejecting transactions if invariants are violated.

ai.description: This file implements the logic for handling validator manifests in the Ripple (XRPL) server. It defines the Manifest and ManifestCache classes, which manage validator key rotation, revocation, and verification. The Manifest class represents a validator manifest, providing methods to verify signatures, check revocation status, and extract signatures. The ManifestCache class maintains a thread-safe cache of manifests, mapping master and signing keys, and provides methods to apply new manifests, check key status, and load/save manifests from/to a database or configuration. The code ensures that only valid, non-stale, and non-conflicting manifests are accepted, and handles revocation and key uniqueness. Utility functions are included for deserializing manifests, loading validator tokens, and logging manifest actions. The file is critical for secure validator key management and trust in the XRPL network.

This file defines a C++ unit test reporter class for the Beast unit test framework, used in the XRPL (Ripple) codebase. The reporter class, derived from runner, tracks and reports the results of test suites and cases, including counts of total and failed tests, and timing information. It outputs results to a provided output stream (defaulting to std::cout), and highlights the longest-running test suites. The class is non-copyable and manages its own state for the current suite and case. It provides hooks for test events (suite/case begin/end, pass, fail, log) and formats output for human readability, including durations and failure reasons. The implementation uses C++ standard library features and Boost utilities.

This file defines a set of smart pointer classes for managing object lifetimes using intrusive reference counting in the Ripple codebase. The main classes are SharedIntrusive (a reference-counted smart pointer), WeakIntrusive (a weak pointer that does not affect the reference count), and SharedWeakUnion (a union type that can hold either a strong or weak reference). The file provides constructors, assignment operators, and utility functions for safe pointer management, including static and dynamic casting, adoption of raw pointers, and reference counting operations. Helper tags and concepts are used to control pointer adoption semantics. The intr_ptr namespace provides type aliases and factory/casting functions for easier usage. These classes are designed to be efficient alternatives to standard smart pointers, tailored for use with objects that implement their own reference counting.

This file implements the core logic for applying, preflighting, and preclaiming transactions in the XRPL (XRP Ledger) server. It provides a generic mechanism to dispatch transaction processing steps based on transaction type using a template function (with_txn_type), which maps transaction types to their corresponding handler classes. The file defines helper functions for evaluating transaction consequences, calculating base fees, and invoking the main transaction lifecycle steps: preflight (initial validation), preclaim (further checks before application), and apply (executing the transaction). It handles unknown transaction types with a custom exception and logs errors appropriately. The file also defines the TxConsequences class, which encapsulates the effects and costs of a transaction. Overall, this file is central to the transaction processing pipeline, ensuring that each transaction type is handled according to its specific logic and that errors are managed robustly.

This file implements the core logic for the 'simulate' RPC handler in the XRPL server. It allows clients to simulate the application of a transaction to the current open ledger without actually submitting it. The main function, doSimulate, processes incoming parameters, validates and parses the transaction (from either JSON or binary blob), autofills missing fields (like Fee, Sequence, SigningPubKey, etc.), and ensures the transaction is unsigned. It then constructs a Transaction object and applies it in 'dry run' mode using the transaction queue, returning the simulated result, including engine result codes, messages, and optional metadata in either JSON or binary format. The code includes robust error handling for malformed input, missing fields, and unsupported transaction types (like batch transactions). The file is structured around several helper functions for autofilling transaction fields, extracting transaction JSON from parameters, and formatting the simulation result.

This file defines the base_uint template class, which represents fixed-size unsigned integers of arbitrary bit length (multiples of 32, at least 64 bits). It provides storage, construction, assignment, and arithmetic/bitwise operations for these integers, as well as parsing from hex strings and conversion to strings. The class is used to implement types like uint128, uint160, uint192, and uint256. The file also includes utility templates for checking if a container is contiguous, and provides comparison, hashing, and stream output operators for base_uint types. The design ensures no padding bytes and supports endian conversions for portability. The file is part of the Ripple/XRPL codebase and is used for cryptographic and protocol identifiers.

This file implements the core logic for handling IOU (I Owe You) amounts in the Ripple (XRPL) protocol. It provides functions and constants for representing, normalizing, and manipulating IOU amounts with high precision, using a mantissa and exponent format. The code includes mechanisms to switch between different number handling strategies, normalization routines to ensure values stay within valid ranges, and arithmetic operations such as addition and ratio multiplication (with rounding options). The mulRatio function uses high-precision arithmetic to safely multiply and divide IOU amounts, handling edge cases like overflow, underflow, and rounding. The file also provides utility functions for string conversion and internal state management. Overall, it ensures accurate and robust handling of non-native currency values in the XRPL system.

It outputs results to a provided output stream (defaulting to std::cout), and highlights the longest-running test suites. The class is non-copyable and manages its own state for the current suite and case. It provides hooks for test events (suite/case begin/end, pass, fail, log) and formats output for human readability, including durations and failure reasons. The implementation uses C++ standard library features and Boost utilities.

The class provides methods to join, detach, swap threads, and query thread properties. When joining, it propagates aborts to the suite. The run method executes the provided function and handles exceptions, reporting failures to the suite if unhandled exceptions occur. This design helps integrate thread management with the unit test framework, ensuring proper error handling and test suite interaction.

It also includes a nested MutableTxSet class for modifying transaction sets (inserting and erasing transactions) before finalizing them. The compare method allows for efficient detection of differences between two transaction sets. These classes are essential for handling transaction sets during the consensus process in the XRPL ledger.

The JobTypes class maintains a map of all job types and their corresponding information, provides singleton access via the instance() method, and offers methods to retrieve job type names, information, and iterators for traversal. The class ensures that each job type is unique and includes a default 'invalid' job type for error handling. The job types cover a wide range of system tasks, including client commands, ledger operations, transaction processing, network operations, and administrative tasks.

The file also defines helper structures and functions for transaction preflight checks, preclaim validation, and application of state changes to the ledger. The file also defines enums for direction and offer crossing, utility functions for working with strands (sequences of steps), and exception handling for flow errors. It provides interfaces for constructing different types of steps (direct, book, XRP endpoint), and a context struct (StrandContext) for managing state during strand construction. The file is central to the pathfinding and payment flow logic in XRPL, enabling flexible and extensible handling of complex payment routes.

This file implements the LedgerHistory class, which manages the caching, retrieval, and validation of ledgers in the XRPL (XRP Ledger) server. It provides mechanisms to insert ledgers into caches, retrieve them by hash or sequence number, and handle mismatches between built and validated ledgers. The class maintains two main caches: one for ledgers by hash and another for consensus-validated ledgers by index. It includes detailed logging and comparison functions to analyze and report differences between ledgers, especially in cases of mismatches during consensus. The file also provides utility functions for cache maintenance, such as clearing old entries and fixing index-to-hash mappings. Overall, LedgerHistory is central to ensuring ledger consistency and diagnosing consensus issues in the XRPL server.

This file implements helper functions for managing and validating credentials in the XRPLedger. It provides logic to check if credentials are expired, remove expired credentials from the ledger, and delete credential ledger entries while updating related account data. The file includes functions to validate credential fields in transactions, check for duplicates, and ensure credentials are properly associated with accounts and accepted. It also verifies if an account has valid credentials for a permissioned domain, checks deposit preauthorization based on credentials, and ensures the integrity and size of credential arrays. The code is focused on maintaining the correctness and security of credential-based operations within the ledger, handling edge cases such as expired or malformed credentials, and enforcing permission checks for sensitive actions.
